ep.share.intro.text: This is Pebble Tortoise. Pebble made this chocolate bar for snack time. It has 8 squares, and 4 friends are going to share it.
ep.share.intro.heard: This is Pebble Tortoise. Pebble made this chocolate bar for snack time. It has eight squares, and four friends are going to share it.

ep.share.plates.text: Here is a plate for each of the 4 friends. Sharing is only fair if every friend gets a piece the same size.
ep.share.plates.heard: Here is a plate for each of the four friends. Sharing is only fair if every friend gets a piece the same size.

ep.share.cut.text: You get to cut the bar for them. Tap between two squares to make a cut. Each cut makes one more piece, and we stop when there are 4 pieces.
ep.share.cut.heard: You get to cut the bar for them. Tap between two squares to make a cut. Each cut makes one more piece, and we stop when there are four pieces.

ep.share.try.you.text: Let's see your cut. Each piece goes onto a plate, and then the pieces stand up side by side, so we can compare them.
ep.share.try.you.heard: Let's see your cut. Each piece goes onto a plate, and then the pieces stand up side by side, so we can compare them.

ep.share.try.again.text: Let's see your new cut. The pieces go onto the plates again, and then they stand up side by side.
ep.share.try.again.heard: Let's see your new cut. The pieces go onto the plates again, and then they stand up side by side.

ep.share.try.together.text: Let's see the pieces we cut together. They go onto the plates, and then they stand up side by side.
ep.share.try.together.heard: Let's see the pieces we cut together. They go onto the plates and then they stand up side by side.

ep.share.try.last.text: Let's see your cut. The pieces go onto the 3 plates, and then they stand up side by side.
ep.share.try.last.heard: Let's see your cut. The pieces go onto the three plates, and then they stand up side by side.

ep.share.fair.text: Your pieces are all the same size, {n} squares each, so no friend gets more chocolate than another. That's a fair share.
ep.share.fair.heard: Your pieces are all the same size, so no friend gets more chocolate than another. That's a fair share.

ep.share.fair.together.text: Now the pieces are all the same size, {n} squares each, so no friend gets more chocolate than another. That's a fair share.
ep.share.fair.together.heard: Now the pieces are all the same size, so no friend gets more chocolate than another. That's a fair share.

ep.share.unfair.text: Your pieces aren't all the same size. Count the squares: the smallest piece has {n} and the biggest has {m}. So one friend would get less chocolate than another, and that isn't fair yet.
ep.share.unfair.heard: Your pieces aren't all the same size. Count the square. The smallest piece has fewer than the biggest. So one friend would get less chocolate than another. And that isn't fair yet.

ep.share.again.text: The pieces go back together into one whole bar. Try cutting it again, so that all {n} pieces have the same number of squares.
ep.share.again.heard: The pieces go back together into one whole bar. Try cutting it again so that all the pieces have the same number of squares.

ep.share.together.text: Cutting pieces that are all the same size is hard to do in one go, so let's do it together in two steps: first 2 pieces the same size, then each of those into 2.
ep.share.together.heard: Cutting pieces that are all the same size is hard to do in one go, so let's do it together in two steps. First two pieces the same size, then each of those into two.

ep.share.half.text: First, cut the bar in half. Halves are 2 pieces the same size, so the cut goes in the middle, with the same number of squares on each side.
ep.share.half.heard: First, cut the bar in half. Halves are two pieces the same size, so the cut goes in the middle, with the same number of squares on each side.

ep.share.half.yes.text: Both halves are {n} squares long, so they're the same size, and that cut is right in the middle.
ep.share.half.yes.heard: Both halves have the same number of squares, so they're the same size, and that cut is right in the middle.

ep.share.eight.half.no.text: Those two pieces are {n} squares and {m} squares, so that cut isn't in the middle. 4 and 4 make 8, so the middle has 4 squares on each side.
ep.share.eight.half.no.heard: Those two pieces aren't the same size, so that cut isn't in the middle. Four and four make eight, so the middle has four squares on each side.

ep.share.eight.quarter.text: Now cut each half in half the same way. Each half is 4 squares long, so its middle has 2 squares on each side. Then all 4 pieces will be the same size.
ep.share.eight.quarter.heard: Now cut each half in half the same way. Each half is four squares long, so its middle has two squares on each side. Then all four pieces will be the same size.

ep.share.quarter.yes.text: That cut is right in the middle of a half, with {n} squares on each side. Now do the same in the other half.
ep.share.quarter.yes.heard: That cut is right in the middle of a half, with the same number of squares on each side. Now do the same in the other half.

ep.share.eight.quarter.no.text: Those pieces aren't the same size, so that cut isn't in the middle of a half. Each half has 4 squares, so its middle has 2 squares on each side.
ep.share.eight.quarter.no.heard: Those pieces aren't the same size, so that cut isn't in the middle of a half. Each half has four squares, so its middle has two squares on each side.

ep.share.twelve.half.no.text: Those two pieces are {n} squares and {m} squares, so that cut isn't in the middle. 6 and 6 make 12, so the middle has 6 squares on each side.
ep.share.twelve.half.no.heard: Those two pieces aren't the same size, so that cut isn't in the middle. Six and six make twelve, so the middle has six squares on each side.

ep.share.twelve.quarter.text: Now cut each half in half the same way. Each half is 6 squares long, so its middle has 3 squares on each side. Then all 4 pieces will be the same size.
ep.share.twelve.quarter.heard: Now cut each half and half the same way. Each half is six squares long, so its middle has three squares on each side. Then all four pieces will be the same size.

ep.share.twelve.quarter.no.text: Those pieces aren't the same size, so that cut isn't in the middle of a half. Each half has 6 squares, so its middle has 3 squares on each side.
ep.share.twelve.quarter.no.heard: Those pieces aren't the same size, so that cut isn't in the middle of a half. Each half has six squares, so its middle has three squares on each side.

ep.share.name.text: These 4 pieces are all the same size, so they are equal pieces. Each one is one of 4 equal pieces, so it is called one fourth, and we write it like this.
ep.share.name.heard: These four pieces are all the same size, so they are equal pieces. Each one is one of four equal pieces, so it is called one-fourth, and we write it like this.

ep.share.name.why.text: The 4 on the bottom says the whole bar was cut into 4 equal pieces. The 1 on top says we mean 1 of those pieces.
ep.share.name.why.heard: The four on the bottom says the whole bar was cut into four equal pieces. The one on top says we mean one of those pieces.

ep.share.try.buddy.text: Now your buddy's idea. Your buddy cuts a bar the same size into 4 pieces, and thinks each piece is one fourth, because there are 4 of them.
ep.share.try.buddy.heard: Now your buddy's idea. Your buddy cuts a bar the same size into four pieces and thinks each piece is one-fourth because there are four of them.

ep.share.buddy.ask.text: Your buddy's bar is the lighter one, at the front. Look at its 4 pieces. Is each of your buddy's pieces one fourth of the bar?
ep.share.buddy.ask.heard: Your buddy's bar is the lighter one, at the front. Look at its four pieces. Is each of your buddy's pieces one-fourth of the bar?

ep.share.try.test.text: Let's test your buddy's pieces. They stand up side by side, next to your fair ones, with how many squares each one has written on it.
ep.share.try.test.heard: Let's test your buddy's pieces. They stand up side by side, next to your fair ones, with how many squares each one has written on it.

ep.share.buddy.yes.text: You said yes, and your buddy's bar does have 4 pieces. But one fourth of this bar is 2 squares, like each of your pieces. Your buddy's are 1, 1, 3 and 3 squares, so none is one fourth.
ep.share.buddy.yes.heard: You said yes, and your buddy's bar does have four pieces. But one-fourth of this bar is two squares, like each of your pieces. Your buddies are one, one-three, and three squares, so none is one-fourth.

ep.share.buddy.no.text: You were right to say no. One fourth of this bar is 2 squares, like each of your pieces. Your buddy's pieces are 1, 1, 3 and 3 squares, so none of them is one fourth.
ep.share.buddy.no.heard: You were right to say no. One-fourth of this bar is two squares, like each of your pieces. Your buddy's pieces are one, one, three, and three squares, so none of them is one-fourth.

ep.share.buddy.why.text: So 4 pieces are not always fourths. They are fourths only when all 4 are the same size.
ep.share.buddy.why.heard: So four pieces are not always fourths. They are fourths only when all four are in the same size.

ep.share.more.text: Pebble wonders what would happen if 8 friends shared a bar the same size. Each piece would be one of 8 equal pieces, so it would be called one eighth, written 1/8.
ep.share.more.heard: Pebble wonders what would happen if eight friends shared a bar the same size. Each piece would be one of eight equal pieces, so it would be called one-eighth.

ep.share.which.text: Pebble thinks one eighth is more chocolate than one fourth, because 8 is more than 4. What do you think? Which piece has more chocolate?
ep.share.which.heard: Pebble thinks one-eighth is more chocolate than one-fourth, because eight is more than four. What do you think? Which piece has more chocolate?

ep.share.try.pal.text: Let's test Pebble's idea. Pebble cuts a bar the same size into 8 equal pieces, and one of them stands next to your fourths, so we can compare them.
ep.share.try.pal.heard: Let's test Pebble's idea. Pebble cuts a bar the same size into eight equal pieces, and one of them stands next to your fourths, so we can compare them.

ep.share.eighth.you.text: You were right: one eighth is less chocolate than one fourth. One eighth is only 1 square, and one fourth is 2 squares.
ep.share.eighth.you.heard: You were right. One-eighth is less chocolate than one-fourth. One-eighth is only one square, and one-fourth is two squares.

ep.share.eighth.pal.text: You and Pebble both picked one eighth, but look: one eighth is only 1 square, and one fourth is 2 squares. One eighth is less chocolate.
ep.share.eighth.pal.heard: You and Pebble both picked 1-8, but look. 1-8 is only one square, and 1-4 is two squares. 1-8 is less chocolate.

ep.share.eighth.same.text: They aren't the same: one eighth is only 1 square, and one fourth is 2 squares. One eighth is less chocolate.
ep.share.eighth.same.heard: They aren't the same. One-eighth is only one square, and one-fourth is two squares. One-eighth is less chocolate.

ep.share.eighth.why.text: 8 is a bigger number than 4, but here it means the same bar was shared by more friends, so each piece had to be smaller. That's why one eighth is less than one fourth.
ep.share.eighth.why.heard: Eight is a bigger number than four, but here it means the same bar was shared by more friends, so each piece had to be smaller. That's why one-eighth is less than one-fourth.

ep.share.last.text: Here's a new bar with 6 squares. This time 3 friends share it: your buddy, Pebble and you. Cut it so all 3 pieces are the same size.
ep.share.last.heard: Here's a new bar with six squares. This time three friends share it. Your buddy, Pebble and you. Cut it so all three pieces are the same size.

ep.share.hint.text: The pieces go back together. Here's a way to find where to cut: 2 and 2 and 2 make 6, so each of the 3 friends can have 2 squares. Try a cut after every 2 squares.
ep.share.hint.heard: The pieces go back together. Here's a way to find where to cut. Two and two and two make six, so each of the three friends can have two squares. Try a cut after every two squares.

ep.share.call.text: Each of you has one piece now, and they're all the same size. What is each piece called?
ep.share.call.heard: Each of you has one piece now, and they're all the same size. What is each piece called?

ep.share.try.name.text: Let's see what 1/{n} of this bar looks like. It stands next to your pieces, so we can compare them.
ep.share.try.name.heard: Let's see what your answers looks like. It stands next to your pieces, so we can compare them.

ep.share.call.squares.text: One sixth would be 1 of 6 equal pieces, and that is only 1 square of this bar. Each of your pieces is 2 squares.
ep.share.call.squares.heard: 1 sixth would be one of six equal pieces, and that is only one square of this bar. Each of your pieces is two squares.

ep.share.call.half.text: One half would be 1 of 2 equal pieces, and that is 3 squares of this bar. Each of your pieces is 2 squares.
ep.share.call.half.heard: One half would be one of two equal pieces, and that is three squares of this bar. Each of your pieces is two squares.

ep.share.call.why.text: The number on the bottom counts the equal pieces the bar was cut into, not its squares. This bar was cut into 3 equal pieces, so each piece is one third, written 1/3.
ep.share.call.why.heard: The number on the bottom counts the equal pieces the bar was cut into, not its squares. This bar was cut into three equal pieces, so each piece is one-third.

ep.share.call.yes.text: Yes. The bar was cut into 3 equal pieces, so each piece is one third, written 1/3. The 3 on the bottom counts the 3 pieces, not the 6 squares.
ep.share.call.yes.heard: Yes, the bar was cut into three equal pieces, so each piece is one-third. The three on the bottom counts the three pieces, not the six squares.

ep.share.try.give.heard: Pebble isn't hungry yet, so Pebble gives its piece to you. Watch! It goes on top of your piece, on your plate.

ep.share.two.ask.heard: So how much of the bar is on your plate?

ep.share.try.six.heard: Let's see what 2 sixths of this bar would be. Here is a bar just like it, cut into six equal pieces, and two of those pieces stand next to your plate.

ep.share.six.show.heard: Two-sixths of the bar is only these two squares. Your plate has four squares, twice as much, so the chocolate on your plate is more than two-sixths.

ep.share.try.two.text: Let's check. Each piece gets its name, and then we count the thirds on your plate.
ep.share.try.two.heard: Let's check. Each piece gets its name, and then we count the thirds on your plate.

ep.share.try.two.together.text: Let's work it out together. Each piece gets its name, and then we count the thirds on your plate.
ep.share.try.two.together.heard: Let's work it out together. Each piece gets its name, and then we count the thirds on your plate.

ep.share.two.yes.text: Yes, two thirds, written 2/3. Each piece is one third, and you have 2 of them. The 2 on top counts the thirds you have.
ep.share.two.yes.heard: Yes, two-thirds. Each piece is one-third, and you have two of them. The two on top counts the thirds you have.

ep.share.two.one.text: One third is only one piece. Your plate has 2 pieces, and each one is one third.
ep.share.two.one.heard: One third is only one piece. Your plate has two pieces and each one is one third.

ep.share.two.six.text: The number on the bottom says how many equal pieces the bar was cut into. Yours was cut into 3, not 6, so each piece is one third.
ep.share.two.six.heard: The number on the bottom says how many equal pieces the bar was cut into. Yours was cut into three, not six, so each piece is one-third.

ep.share.two.top.heard: The number on top counts the pieces you have. You have two thirds, so the top number is two.

ep.share.own.ask.heard: Your buddy is about to eat its piece. How much of the bar is your buddy's piece?

ep.share.own.yes.text: Yes, one third. The bar was cut into 3 equal pieces, and your buddy has 1 of them.

ep.share.eat.heard: Now your buddy eats its third of the bar. Your two-thirds stay on your plate. Two pieces, each one the same size as your buddy's piece.

ep.share.check.heard: Here's a bar with 12 squares and four friends will share it. Cut it so every friend gets a piece the same size.

ep.share.check.call.text: Each friend has one piece now. What is each piece called?
ep.share.check.call.heard: Each friend has one piece now. What is each piece called?

ep.share.check.call.yes.heard: Yes. The bar was cut into four equal pieces, so each one is one-fourth, even though this bar has 12 squares.

ep.count.intro.text: This is Sprout Bunny. Sprout Bunny baked cookies for a party, and each cookie needs its own plate to sit on.
ep.count.intro.heard: This is Sprout Bunny. Sprout Bunny baked cookies for a party, and each cookie needs its own plate to sit on.

ep.count.need.text: To get out the right number of plates, we need to know how many cookies there are. So let's count them.
ep.count.need.heard: To get out the right number of plates, we need to know how many cookies there are. So let's count them.

ep.count.try.demo.text: Watch. I touch one cookie and say one number. Then I move that cookie to the front, so I know it's counted.
ep.count.try.demo.heard: Watch. I touch one cookie and say one number. Then I move that cookie to the front, so I know it's counted.

ep.count.demo.last.text: 1, 2, 3. The last number I said was 3, so there are 3 cookies. The last number you say when you count tells you how many.
ep.count.demo.last.heard: One, two, three. The last number I said was three, so there are three cookies. The last number you say when you count tells you how many.

ep.count.turn.heard: Now it's your turn with more cookies. Tap each cookie one time. It moves to the front and gets the next number.

ep.count.how.text: You touched every cookie, and each one has its own number. How many cookies are there?
ep.count.how.heard: You touched every cookie, and each one has its own number. How many cookies are there?

ep.count.try.you.text: You said {n}. Let's get that many plates, and put one cookie on each plate.
ep.count.try.you.heard: Let's get as many plates as you said, and put one cookie on each plate.

ep.count.right.text: Your {n} plates are just right! Every cookie has a plate, and no plate is empty.
ep.count.right.heard: Your plates are just right. Every cookie has a plate, and no plate is empty.

ep.count.few.text: Your {n} plates weren't enough. Look, a cookie is left with no plate, so there are more cookies than plates.
ep.count.few.heard: Your plates weren't enough. Look, a cookie is left with no plate, so there are more cookies than that.

ep.count.over.text: Your {n} plates were too many. Look, a plate is left empty, so there are fewer cookies than plates.
ep.count.over.heard: Your plates were too many. Look, a plate is left empty, so there are fewer cookies than that.

ep.count.try.zero.text: Your number is 0. Let's see what 0 plates looks like.
ep.count.try.zero.heard: Your number is zero. Let's see what zero plates looks like.

ep.count.zero.text: Zero means no plates at all, so not one cookie has a plate to sit on. We can see cookies right here, so there are more than zero.
ep.count.zero.heard: Zero means no plates at all, so not one cookie has a plate to sit on. We can see cookies right here, so there are more than zero.

ep.count.b5.why.text: The last cookie you counted got the number 5, so there are 5 cookies. The last number you say tells you how many.
ep.count.b5.why.heard: The last cookie you counted got the number 5, so there are 5 cookies. The last number you say tells you how many.

ep.count.b5.show.text: Let's look at the numbers together. Each cookie got one number: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. The last number is 5, so there are 5 cookies.
ep.count.b5.show.heard: Let's look at the numbers together. Each cookie got one number. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. The last number is 5, so there are 5 cookies.

ep.count.try.b5.text: So let's get out 5 plates, one for each cookie.
ep.count.try.b5.heard: So let's get out 5 plates, one for each cookie.

ep.count.fit.text: Now every cookie has a plate, and no plate is empty.
ep.count.fit.heard: Now every cookie has a plate, and no plate is empty.

ep.count.mixed.text: Sprout Bunny baked some more cookies. These ones are all over the tray, so it's hard to remember which ones you've counted.
ep.count.mixed.heard: Sprout Bunny baked some more cookies. These ones are all over the tray, so it's hard to remember which ones you've counted.

ep.count.try.pal.text: Watch Sprout Bunny count them. Each cookie Sprout Bunny counts gets a number.
ep.count.try.pal.heard: Watch Sprout Bunny count them. Each Cookie Sprout Bunny counts gets a number.

ep.count.pal.find.heard: Sprout Bunny counted eight, but one cookie got two numbers. Can you find it? Tap the cookie that has two numbers.

ep.count.find.no.two.heard: That cookie has just one number on it. Look for the cookie that has two numbers.

ep.count.pal.found.heard: You found it. Sprout Bunny counted this cookie twice, so it got two numbers. That is one number too many, so there are not eight cookies.

ep.count.try.buddy.heard: Now watch your buddy count them.

ep.count.buddy.find.heard: Your buddy counted six, but one cookie got no number. Can you find it? Tap the cookie that has no number.

ep.count.buddy.shown.heard: It's hard to spot, so here it is with the red ring. Your buddy skipped this cookie, so it got no number. It was never counted, so there are more than six cookies.

ep.count.move.text: So let's move each cookie to the front as we count it, like before. Tap each cookie one time.
ep.count.move.heard: So let's move each cookie to the front as we count it, like before. Tap each cookie one time.

ep.count.how2.text: Every cookie is at the front now, and each one has one number. How many cookies are there?
ep.count.how2.heard: Every cookie is at the front now, and each one has one number. How many cookies are there?

ep.count.b7.why.text: The last cookie you counted got the number 7, so there are 7 cookies. That's not 8 and not 6, because each cookie got just one number.
ep.count.b7.why.heard: The last cookie you counted got the number 7, so there are 7 cookies. That's not 8 and not 6, because each cookie got just one number.

ep.count.b7.show.text: Let's look at the numbers together. This time each cookie got just one number: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7. The last number is 7, so there are 7 cookies, not 8 and not 6.
ep.count.b7.show.heard: Let's look at the numbers together. This time, each cookie got just one number. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7. The last number is 7, so there are 7 cookies, not 8 and not 6.

ep.count.try.b7.text: So let's get out 7 plates, one for each cookie.
ep.count.try.b7.heard: So let's get out seven plates, one for each cookie.

ep.count.try.bump.text: Uh oh, Sprout Bunny bumps the table. Watch what happens to the cookies.
ep.count.try.bump.heard: Uh-oh. Sprout Bunny bumps the table. Watch what happens to the cookies.

ep.count.moved.text: The cookies slid all around the tray, and their numbers are gone. How many cookies are there now?
ep.count.moved.heard: The cookies slid all around the tray and their numbers are gone. How many cookies are there now?

ep.count.moved.right.text: Yes, there are still 7! The cookies only moved, and moving them doesn't add any or take any away.
ep.count.moved.right.heard: Yes, there are still seven. The cookies only moved, and moving them doesn't add any or take any away.

ep.count.try.recount.again.text: Let's count them again. This time each cookie stays where it is, and its number shows it's been counted. Tap each cookie one time, starting with any cookie you like.
ep.count.try.recount.again.heard: Let's count them again. This time, each cookie stays where it is, and its number shows it's been counted. Tap each cookie one time, starting with any cookie you like.

ep.count.recount.why.text: The last number is 7 again. The cookies only moved, and moving them doesn't add any or take any away. So there are still 7, wherever they sit.
ep.count.recount.why.heard: The last number is seven again. The cookies only moved, and moving them doesn't add any or take any away. So there are still seven, wherever they sit.

ep.count.try.party.text: There are 7 cookies, so Sprout Bunny gets out 7 plates, one for each cookie, to take them to the party.
ep.count.try.party.heard: There are seven cookies, so Sprout Bunny gets out seven plates, one for each cookie, to take them to the party.

ep.count.off.text: Every cookie has its own plate, with no cookie left out and no plate left empty. Sprout Bunny is off to the party!
ep.count.off.heard: Every cookie has its own plate, with no cookie left out and no plate left empty. Sprout Bunny is off to the party.

ep.count.off.extra.text: There are 4 cookies and 4 plates, one plate for each cookie. Sprout Bunny is off to the party with them!
ep.count.off.extra.heard: There are four cookies and four plates, one plate for each cookie. Sprout Bunny is off to the party with them.

ep.count.extra.text: Those cookies are put away. Sprout Bunny found a few more cookies in the oven, and these need counting too. Tap each cookie one time.
ep.count.extra.heard: Those cookies are put away. Sprout Bunny found a few more cookies in the oven, and these need counting too. Tap each cookie one time.

ep.count.how.last.text: You touched every cookie. Look at the cookie you tapped last and read its number. How many cookies are there?
ep.count.how.last.heard: You touched every cookie. Look at the cookie you tapped last and read its number. How many cookies are there?

ep.count.b4.why.text: The last cookie you counted got the number 4, so there are 4 cookies. You counted them all by yourself.
ep.count.b4.why.heard: The last cookie you counted got the number four, so there are four cookies. You counted them all by yourself.

ep.count.b4.show.text: Let's look at the numbers together. Each cookie got one number: 1, 2, 3, 4. The last number is 4, so there are 4 cookies.
ep.count.b4.show.heard: Let's look at the numbers together. Each cookie got one number. One, two, three, four. The last number is four, so there are four cookies.

ep.count.try.b4.text: So let's get out 4 plates, one for each cookie.
ep.count.try.b4.heard: So let's get out four plates, one for each cookie.

ep.count.check.text: Here are some new cookies for Sprout Bunny's party, all over the tray. Tap each cookie one time to count it.
ep.count.check.heard: Here are some new cookies for Sprout Bunny's party. All over the tray. Tap each cookie one time to count it.

ep.count.b6.why.text: The last cookie you counted got the number 6, so there are 6 cookies. The last number you say tells you how many.
ep.count.b6.why.heard: The last cookie you counted got the number 6, so there are 6 cookies. The last number you say tells you how many.

ep.count.b6.show.text: Let's look at the numbers together. Each cookie got one number: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. The last number is 6, so there are 6 cookies.
ep.count.b6.show.heard: Let's look at the numbers together. Each cookie got one number. One, two, three, four, five, six. The last number is six, so there are six cookies.

ep.count.try.b6.text: So let's get out 6 plates, one for each cookie.
ep.count.try.b6.heard: So let's get out six plates, one for each cookie.

ep.eq.intro.text: This is the Comet Cat. It filled two bags with star sand, the same amount in each, and it has a puzzle for you: how heavy is one bag?
ep.eq.intro.heard: This is the Comet Cat. It filled two bags with star sand, the same amount in each, and it has a puzzle for you. How heavy is one bag?

ep.eq.scale.text: Here is the puzzle. The two bags and 3 loose weights go on one side of a balance. Every weight is the same. Watch the other side as weights go on, one at a time.
ep.eq.scale.heard: Here is the puzzle. The two bags and three loose weights go on one side of a balance. Every weight is the same. Watch the other side as weights go on, one at a time.

ep.eq.level.text: With 11 weights it hangs level. Level means both sides weigh the same, so the two bags and the 3 loose weights together weigh as much as 11 weights.
ep.eq.level.heard: With 11 weights it hangs level. Level means both sides weigh the same, so the two bags and the three loose weights together weigh as much as 11 weights.

ep.eq.letter.text: The Comet Cat wrote x on each bag. x stands for how many weights one bag weighs: a number we don't know yet. Both bags say x because they weigh the same.
ep.eq.letter.heard: The comet cat wrote X on each bag. X stands for how many weights one bag weighs, a number we don't know yet. Both bags say X because they weigh the same.

ep.eq.guess.text: How many weights do you think one bag weighs? Make a guess. Any guess can be tested on the balance.
ep.eq.guess.heard: How many weights do you think one bag weighs? Make a guess. Any guess can be tested on the balance.

ep.eq.try.you.text: Let's test {n}. Each bag comes off, and that many weights go in its place. If one bag really weighs that much, it will still hang level.
ep.eq.try.you.heard: Let's test your number. Each bag comes off, and that many weights go in its place. If one bag really weighs that much, it will still hang level.

ep.eq.try.again.text: Let's test {n} in each bag's place.
ep.eq.try.again.heard: Let's test your number in each bag's place.

ep.eq.heavy.text: With {n} in place of each bag, the bags' side comes to {m} weights. That's more than the {k} on the other side, and the heavier side goes down. So one bag weighs less than {n}.
ep.eq.heavy.heard: With your number in place of each bag, the bag's side comes to more weights than the other side has, and the heavier side goes down. So one bag weighs less than your number.

ep.eq.light.text: With {n} in place of each bag, the bags' side comes to {m} weights. That's less than the {k} on the other side, and the lighter side goes up. So one bag weighs more than {n}.
ep.eq.light.heard: With your number in place of each bag, the bag's side comes to fewer weights than the other side has, and the lighter side goes up. So one bag weighs more than your number.

ep.eq.lucky.text: With 4 in each bag's place, it stayed level: 4 and 4 and 3 make 11, so you found it. Now let's find it without guessing, for numbers that are hard to guess.
ep.eq.lucky.heard: With four in each bag's place, it stayed level. Four and four and three make eleven, so you found it. Now let's find it without guessing, for numbers that are hard to guess.

ep.eq.unlucky.text: Guessing can take a lot of tries, so let's work it out instead, one step at a time, by taking things off the balance.
ep.eq.unlucky.heard: Guessing can take a lot of tries, so let's work it out instead, one step at a time, by taking things off the balance.

ep.eq.own.why.text: If one bag sat on its side alone and the balance hung level, we could count the weights on the other side to see how heavy the bag is. So we want a bag on its own.
ep.eq.own.why.heard: If one bag sat on its side alone and the balance hung level, we could count the weights on the other side to see how heavy the bag is. So we want a bag on its own.

ep.eq.try.off.text: First the 3 loose weights come off the bags' side only. Drag them off, and watch what the balance does.
ep.eq.try.off.heard: First, the three loose weights come off the bag's side only. Drag them off, and watch what the balance does.

ep.eq.off.up.text: The bags' side went up. You took 3 weights off it and nothing off the other side, so the bags' side is lighter now, and the lighter side goes up.
ep.eq.off.up.heard: The bag's side went up. You took three weights off it and nothing off the other side, so the bag's side is lighter now, and the lighter side goes up.

ep.eq.other.ask.text: The two sides weighed the same before. How many weights must come off the other side to make it level again?
ep.eq.other.ask.heard: The two sides weighed the same before. How many weights must come off the other side to make it level again?

ep.eq.try.other.text: Let's take your {n} off the other side.
ep.eq.try.other.heard: Let's take your number off the other side.

ep.eq.other.yes.text: Level again. Both sides lost 3 weights, so they still weigh the same. 11 take away 3 is 8, so the two bags together weigh as much as 8 weights.
ep.eq.other.yes.heard: Level again. Both sides lost three weights, so they still weigh the same. Eleven take away three is eight, so the two bags together weigh as much as eight weights.

ep.eq.other.few.text: Your {n} wasn't enough: the other side is still heavier, so it stays down. The bags' side lost 3, so the other side has to lose 3 too.
ep.eq.other.few.heard: Your number wasn't enough. The other side is still heavier, so it stays down. The bag side lost three, so the other side has to lose three too.

ep.eq.other.many.text: Your {n} was too many: now the other side is lighter, so it went up. The bags' side lost 3, so the other side has to lose 3 too.
ep.eq.other.many.heard: Your number was too many. Now the other side is lighter, so it went up. The bag side lost three, so the other side has to lose three too.

ep.eq.other.fix.text: With 3 off the other side, it's level again, because both sides lost the same. 11 take away 3 is 8, so the two bags together weigh as much as 8 weights.
ep.eq.other.fix.heard: With three off the other side, it's level again because both sides lost the same. Eleven take away three is eight, so the two bags together weigh as much as eight weights.

ep.eq.share.idea.text: Next, one of the two bags comes off. The bags weigh the same, so that is half of the bags' side. Both sides weigh the same, so half of one side weighs as much as half of the other.
ep.eq.share.idea.heard: Next, one of the two bags comes off. The bags weigh the same, so that is half of the bag's side. Both sides weigh the same, so half of one side weighs as much as half of the other.

ep.eq.share.ask.text: How many weights must come off the other side with the bag, so the balance stays level?
ep.eq.share.ask.heard: How many weights must come off the other side with the bag so the balance stays level?

ep.eq.try.share.text: Let's take one bag off, and {n} off the other side, as you said.
ep.eq.try.share.heard: Let's take one bag off, and your number off the other side.

ep.eq.share.yes.text: It stayed level with 4. The two bags weigh the same, so one bag is half of the bags' side, and half of the 8 weights is 4. So x is 4.
ep.eq.share.yes.heard: It stayed level with four. The two bags weigh the same, so one bag is half of the bag side, and half of the eight weights is four. So X is four.

ep.eq.share.few.text: Your {n} wasn't enough. The other side still has {m} weights and it went down, so {m} weights are heavier than the one bag that's left.
ep.eq.share.few.heard: Your number wasn't enough. The other side went down, so the weights still on it are heavier than the one bag that's left.

ep.eq.share.many.text: Your {n} was too many. The other side has only {m} weights left and it went up, so {m} weights are lighter than the one bag that's left.
ep.eq.share.many.heard: Your number was too many. The other side went up, so the weights still on it are lighter than the one bag that's left.

ep.eq.share.how.text: Let's put them back. Here's a way to be sure: the two bags weigh the same, so the 8 weights are shared into 2 equal piles, one for each bag.
ep.eq.share.how.heard: Let's put them back. Here's a way to be sure. The two bags weigh the same, so the eight weights are shared into two equal piles, one for each bag.

ep.eq.share.done.text: Each pile has 4. It stayed level when one bag and one pile came off, so the one bag left weighs as much as the one pile of 4 left. That means x is 4.
ep.eq.share.done.heard: Each pile has four. It stayed level when one bag and one pile came off, so the one bag left weighs as much as the one pile of four left. That means x is four.

ep.eq.write.text: Here is what we did, written down. The first line is the balance at the start: 2x means the two bags that each weigh x, the 3 is the loose weights, and 11 is the other side.
ep.eq.write.heard: Here is what we did written down. The first line is the balance at the start. 2x means the two bags that each weigh x, the 3 is the loose weights, and 11 is the other side.

ep.eq.write.read.text: The = sign means the two sides weigh the same. Taking 3 off both sides gave 2x = 8. Then keeping half of each side gave x = 4.
ep.eq.write.read.heard: The equals sign means the two sides weigh the same. Taking three off both sides gave 2x equals 8. Then keeping half of each side gave x equals 4.

ep.eq.b.in.text: Here is the next puzzle: three new bags, all the same, and 6 loose weights. Together they weigh as much as 21 weights. Your buddy has an idea for this one.
ep.eq.b.in.heard: Here is the next puzzle. Three new bags, all the same, and six loose weights. Together they weigh as much as 21 weights. Your buddy has an idea for this one.

ep.eq.b.idea.text: Your buddy wants to get to one bag in one step. There are 3 bags, so your buddy keeps 1 bag of the 3, and 7 of the 21 weights, because 21 shared into 3 is 7.
ep.eq.b.idea.heard: Your buddy wants to get to one bag in one step. There are three bags, so your buddy keeps one bag of the three, and seven of the 21 weights, because 21 shared into three is seven.

ep.eq.b.ask.text: Will your buddy's way keep it level? Say what you think before we try it.
ep.eq.b.ask.heard: Will your buddy's way keep it level? Say what you think before we try it.

ep.eq.try.buddy.text: Let's try your buddy's idea. Two bags come off the bags' side, and 14 weights come off the other side, because 21 take away 7 is 14. The 6 loose weights stay where they are.
ep.eq.try.buddy.heard: Let's try your buddy's idea. Two bags come off the bag side and 14 weights come off the other side because 21 take away 7 is 14. The six loose weights stay where they are.

ep.eq.b.no.text: You said it would tip, and it did: the bags' side went down, so that side is heavier now.
ep.eq.b.no.heard: You said it would tip, and it did. The bag side went down, so that side is heavier now.

ep.eq.b.yes.text: You said it would stay level, but it tipped: the bags' side went down, so that side is heavier now.
ep.eq.b.yes.heard: You said it would stay level, but it tipped. The bag's side went down, so that side is heavier now.

ep.eq.b.kept.text: Your buddy kept a third of the bags and a third of the other side, but all 6 of the loose weights. So the bags' side kept too much.
ep.eq.b.kept.heard: Your buddy kept a third of the bags and a third of the other side, but all six of the loose weights. So the bag's side kept too much.

ep.eq.b.rule.text: Sharing a side into 3 means sharing every part of it, the loose weights as well as the bags. It's simpler to take the loose weights off both sides first. Then only bags are left to share.
ep.eq.b.rule.heard: Sharing a side into three means sharing every part of it, the loose weights, as well as the bags. It's simpler to take the loose weights off both sides first. Then only bags are left to share.

ep.eq.b.own.text: Let's put it back. Now it's yours: how heavy is one bag? Do the two steps in your head. First the loose weights come off both sides, then each side is shared into 3.
ep.eq.b.own.heard: Let's put it back. Now it's yours. How heavy is one bag? Do the two steps in your head. First the loose weights come off both sides, then each side is shared into three.

ep.eq.try.both.text: Drag the loose weights off the bags' side, and take the same number off the other side, so the balance stays level.
ep.eq.try.both.heard: Drag the loose weights off the bag's side and take the same number off the other side so the balance stays level.

ep.eq.b.right.text: With 5 in each bag's place, it stayed level: 5 and 5 and 5 and 6 make 21. 6 off both sides leaves 15, and 15 shared into 3 is 5.
ep.eq.b.right.heard: With 5 in each bag's place, it stayed level. 5 and 5 and 5 and 6 make 21. 6 off both sides leaves 15, and 15 shared into 3 is 5.

ep.eq.b.mid.text: Both sides lost 6 weights, so it's still level. 21 take away 6 is 15, so the three bags on their own weigh as much as 15 weights.
ep.eq.b.mid.heard: Both sides lost six weights, so it's still level. 21 takeaway, six is 15, so the three bags on their own weigh as much as 15 weights.

ep.eq.b.share.text: The three bags weigh the same, so the 15 weights are shared into 3 equal piles, one for each bag.
ep.eq.b.share.heard: The three bags weigh the same, so the 15 weights are shared into three equal piles, one for each bag.

ep.eq.b.piles.text: Each pile has 5, so one bag weighs as much as one pile: 5 weights. You can check: 5 and 5 and 5 and 6 make 21.
ep.eq.b.piles.heard: Each pile has five, so one bag weighs as much as one pile. Five weights. You can check. Five and five and five and six make 21.

ep.eq.b.write.text: Written down, it's the same two steps as before: 6 off both sides gave 3x = 15, and sharing each side into 3 gave x = 5.
ep.eq.b.write.heard: Written down, it's the same two steps as before. Six off both sides gave 3x equals 15, and sharing each side into 3 gave x equals 5.

ep.eq.together.text: Let's do this one together with the two steps, starting with the loose weights.
ep.eq.together.heard: Let's do this one together. With the two steps, starting with the loose weights.

ep.eq.b.seven.text: With 7 in place of each bag, the bags' side comes to 27, more than the 21 on the other side. 7 is 21 shared into 3, but the 6 loose weights weren't taken off first.
ep.eq.b.seven.heard: With 7 in place of each bag, the bag's side comes to 27, more than the 21 on the other side. 7 is 21 shared into 3, but the 6 loose weights weren't taken off first.

ep.eq.d.in.text: One more puzzle: four new bags and 1 loose weight weigh as much as 13 weights. We'll do the first step together, and the last step is yours.
ep.eq.d.in.heard: One more puzzle. Four new bags and one loose weight weigh as much as 13 weights. We'll do the first step together, and the last step is yours.

ep.eq.try.d.text: Drag the 1 loose weight off the bags' side, and 1 off the other side, so it stays level.
ep.eq.try.d.heard: Drag the one loose weight off the bag side and one off the other side so it stays level.

ep.eq.d.mid.text: Both sides lost 1, so it's still level. 13 take away 1 is 12, so the four bags on their own weigh as much as 12 weights.
ep.eq.d.mid.heard: Both sides lost one, so it's still level. Thirteen take away one is twelve, so the four bags on their own weigh as much as twelve weights.

ep.eq.d.last.text: Share the 12 weights into 4 equal piles in your head, one pile for each bag. How heavy is one bag?
ep.eq.d.last.heard: Share the 12 weights into 4 equal piles in your head. One pile for each bag. How heavy is one bag?

ep.eq.d.own.text: With 3 in each bag's place, it stayed level: 3 and 3 and 3 and 3 make 12. You shared the 12 into 4 on your own.
ep.eq.d.own.heard: With three in each bag's place, it stayed level. Three and three and three and three make twelve. You shared the twelve into four on your own.

ep.eq.d.share.text: Here is the last step on the balance: the 12 weights are shared into 4 equal piles, one for each bag.
ep.eq.d.share.heard: Here is the last step on the balance. The 12 weights are shared into four equal piles, one for each bag.

ep.eq.d.piles.text: Each pile has 3, so one bag weighs as much as one pile: 3 weights. You can check: 3 and 3 and 3 and 3 and the 1 make 13.
ep.eq.d.piles.heard: Each pile has three, so one bag weighs as much as one pile. Three weights, you can check. Three and three and three and three, and the one make thirteen.

ep.eq.end.text: You found how heavy the bags are, so the Comet Cat writes each number on its tag. The x on each bag was just a number we didn't know yet, and now we do.
ep.eq.end.heard: You found how heavy the bags are, so the Comet Cat writes each number on its tag. The X on each bag was just a number we didn't know yet, and now we do.

ep.eq.end.we.text: Now we know how heavy every bag is, so the Comet Cat writes each number on its tag. The x on each bag was just a number we didn't know yet, and now we do.
ep.eq.end.we.heard: Now we know how heavy every bag is, so the comet cat writes each number on its tag. The X on each bag was just a number we didn't know yet, and now we do.

ep.eq.check.text: Two bags and 5 loose weights weigh as much as 17 weights. How heavy is one bag? Work it out, and the balance will test your answer.
ep.eq.check.heard: Two bags and five loose weights weigh as much as 17 weights. How heavy is one bag? Work it out, and the balance will test your answer.

ep.eq.check.right.text: With 6 in each bag's place, it stayed level: 6 and 6 and 5 make 17. 5 off both sides leaves 12, and half of 12 is 6.
ep.eq.check.right.heard: With six in each bag's place, it stayed level. Six and six and five make seventeen. Five off both sides leaves twelve, and half of twelve is six.

ep.eq.check.again.text: Not level, so one bag isn't that. In your head, take the 5 loose weights off both sides, then take half of what's left on the other side. How heavy is one bag?
ep.eq.check.again.heard: Not level, so one bag isn't that. In your head, take the five loose weights off both sides, then take half of what's left on the other side. How heavy is one bag?

ep.eq.check.mid.text: Both sides lost 5 weights, so it's still level. 17 take away 5 is 12, so the two bags on their own weigh as much as 12 weights.
ep.eq.check.mid.heard: Both sides lost five weights, so it's still level. 17 take away, 5 is 12, so the two bags on their own weigh as much as 12 weights.

ep.eq.check.share.text: The two bags weigh the same, so the 12 weights are shared into 2 equal piles, one for each bag.
ep.eq.check.share.heard: The two bags weigh the same, so the 12 weights are shared into two equal piles, one for each bag.

ep.eq.check.piles.text: Each pile has 6, so one bag weighs 6 weights. You can check: 6 and 6 and 5 make 17.
ep.eq.check.piles.heard: Each pile has six, so one bag weighs six weights. You can check. Six and six and five make 17.
